title: ssh: Adjust length warning for modes that do not encrypt packet length
description:
RFC 4253 6: "[T]he length of the concatenation of 'packet_lVength',
'padding_length', 'payload', and 'random padding' MUST be `a multiple
of the cipher block size or 8, whichever is larger,... even when
using stream ciphers."

Modes that do not encrypt plen with the same key as the other three
cannot follow this as written and delete 'packet_length' from the
above sentence. As padding_length is one byte and random_padding at
least four, packet_length must be at least 8 in all modes.

This is not really necessary for AES GCM, because the block size is
16, but does affect some other modes such as -etm modes or ChaCha20.

We could do different tests based on the negotiated cipher suite later. I would guess that adding support for the -etm modes (decryption and mac verification will fail with them currently) would be higher priority.

Hi John    

From my side out of *-etm@openssh.com (and really not because I wrote some parts of it), I prefer the code + comments which check the minimum packet length depending on the cipher (and related explanations) than an arbitrary value tried to be justified by RFC4253 which do not cover newer packet constructions used by stream ciphers like chacha20-poly1305 or aes**-gcm (=> talking here of 2 to 3 constructions on 4 possible)    
So maybe I would suggest to make a sort of merge of both comments and code checks, that will really help people reading / understanding the code and why it's implemented like this.    

Kind regards
nbanba

I would say really that there's only two possible cases. RFC 4253 requires that the padding be at least 4 octets, and that the block length be treated as being at least 8 even for stream ciphers.

The two cases are whether the the packet length field is encrypted along with the padding_length, payload, and padding, or whether it is not. If packet_length is encrypted along with the padding length, then the total packet length is at least 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 and a multiple of the block size (and thus at least two blocks for the minimum block size of 4), and the value in the packet length field (which does not count itself) is thus `(b - 4) mod b`, which is 12 for the common block sizes of 8 and 16, larger for larger block sizes (but for an unusual block size could be smaller, such as 8 for a block size of 96 bits / 12 bytes.)

If the packet_length is not encrypted along with the others, then the value of packet_length (the concatenation of the length of the other three) is at least 4 + 1 = 5 and a multiple of the block size, and thus at least 8. This covers AES-GCM and all the -etm modes. It happens that for AES the block size is 16, so in fact for AES-GCM and most of the actually used -etm modes the minimum size is 16. For chacha20-poly1305 as a stream cipher it's 8, though the specification *could* have been written to maintain the block size. (It's unimportant for this calculation that there the packet_length is actually encrypted with a separate key.)
So I suppose there's two cases, but those can be split into more precise measurements based on the block size.

I think there is also another point to fix:

That is a different issue and indicates that certain SSH message types are not being parsed by the dissector.

Right, all the undecoded expert infos just indicate that the dissector needs to be extended. pty-req is moderately complicated.

`shell` doesn't need anything because there aren't any more bytes in that message.

> Also I forgot to parse in last MR PING / PONG messages

Do you have a sample of this where the PING and PONG is not dissected? Normally it is, though only if negotiated. I suspect the issue here is that you're clearing `peer_data->global_data->ext_ping_openssh_offered = false;` and it may be the case that implementations do not re-negotiate extensions following a rekey.

I made a lot of tests (tried to cover a maximum of cases) and it's appears that after a REKEY, I didn't get any `ping` 'extension information' after the first msg_code 31 (in clear)   

![Capture_d_écran_du_2025-06-19_17-49-03](/uploads/1847120a15119a4f0e5b923e9b4e266b/Capture_d_écran_du_2025-06-19_17-49-03.png)   

It's possible that the extension would be renegociate later but I didn't find the rule at the moment.    

What do you think about removing line in the KEXINIT block ? 
```c
peer_data->global_data->ext_ping_openssh_offered = false;
```

Not sure it's the best thing to do, for me ping extension should be renegociate at each REKEY but it seems indeed it's nor working like that    
(removing this line allow dissection of PING PONG msg after a rekey but didn't test on a capture of more that 2h)

https://bugzilla.mindrot.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2929

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8308#section-2.4

RFC 8308 implies that SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO is sent only at the beginning of a connection, see the references to after the "first SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS". I don't think that supported extensions are expected to change when re-keying, so I think that line should be deleted.

Thanks for answer, it seems I didn't read well https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8308#section-2.4 , sorry     

I will fix it
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20284 would fix pin pong message dissection after a REKEY event occurs.

But there is still an issue in the dissection:    

After the payload first byte : msg_code c0 (192) or c1 (193), the payload carried message is length prefixed so it have the form:    
packet_length(4) + padding_length(1) + payload_msg_code(1) + rest_of_payload_length_prefix(4) + "rest_of_payload(5)" + padding_string(padding_length)     

So real payload is :    
payload_msg_code(1) + rest_of_payload_length_prefix(4)+  rest_of_payload(5)    
which is not properly dissected right now and we have an expert info PI_UNDECODED for the mismatch between the packet_length and the decoded message "rest_of_payload(5)"   

See: 
![Capture_d_écran_du_2025-06-20_11-53-22](/uploads/82622f708ab3dbe38167c6efb7c57d4b/Capture_d_écran_du_2025-06-20_11-53-22.png)

from: 
[pingpong_rekey.pcapng](/uploads/e34612ccbeb0e321c2cd05dd4c8683f5/pingpong_rekey.pcapng)

Will have a deeper look

In this line:

`dissected_len = ssh_dissect_local_extension(payload_tvb, pinfo, 0, peer_data, msg_type_tree, msg_code) - offset;`

`offset` shouldn't be subtracted, since the subset `payload_tvb` is passed in and the local extension dissection starts at 0, so what is returned is already a dissected length relative to 0.
